learningObjective: State the safety conditions under which a loop-invariant computation can be hoisted out of a loop.

canonicalClaims.claim: Loop-Invariant Code Motion (LICM) may hoist a loop-invariant expression to the preheader only when (1) it is loop-invariant, (2) hoisting preserves dominance of uses, and (3) speculative execution in the preheader introduces no new faults or observable side effects.
conditions: The loop has a well-defined preheader dominating the loop header.
Fault/side-effect semantics of the target IR are known (e.g., division-by-zero traps).
Alias analysis suffices for hoisting loads over intervening stores.
nonImplications: Does not imply hoisting always improves performance; register pressure and spills can offset benefits.
Does not imply LICM is only for arithmetic; loads and calls (with attributes) can also be hoisted.

misconceptions.claim: Any loop-invariant expression can be hoisted without further conditions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Hoisting an expression that may fault (division by zero, out-of-bounds load) introduces a new fault when the loop's trip count is zero; speculative-safety must be established.

misconceptions.claim: LICM only applies to arithmetic operations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Loads and calls can be hoisted with appropriate alias/attribute proof; LLVM's LICM handles all speculatable instructions.

misconceptions.claim: Hoisting an invariant load is safe if no writes occur inside the loop.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In addition, one must consider concurrent modifications (if the language allows), and safety of speculating the load itself (dereferenceable-ness, alignment).
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: LLVM alias analysis and speculatable semantics

implementationFacts: LLVM's LICM uses `isSafeToExecuteUnconditionally` to check speculative-safety.
Loop rotation may precede LICM to create a loop preheader.
For divisions, LICM requires known non-zero divisor (constant, range analysis, or `!range` metadata).
performanceScenarios: Hoisting expensive divisions or memory loads out of hot loops is a significant classic optimization; safety proofs are often the bottleneck.
